items.title: OpenAI closes $11B in new funding at a $1.25T valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has closed an initial $11 billion in new funding at a $1.25 trillion valuation, Bloomberg reported — only the first tranche of a round originally pitched at up to $30 billion, now targeted at about $20 billion, with the rest expected in the coming weeks. Reuters, citing two investors, says SoftBank and MGX took part, with a UAE consortium among the largest participants. The valuation is about 47% above the $852 billion post-money figure from March, but well below the roughly $1.4 trillion originally pitched in September; October reporting also suggested the $1.25 trillion may be a pre-money figure, so the basis is not settled. OpenAI has not publicly confirmed the closing.

items.title: Thinking Machines debuts Inkling 2 Small, a model that trains other models, amid a reported $5B raise
items.summary: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small late on Nov 5: a 594B-parameter MoE with about 17B active per token, built for coding, visual tasks and autonomous research. The company says it doubled an open-source model's weather-forecasting score in 4.5 hours by fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B, and completed initial pre-training in 68 hours on a GB300 NVL72 cluster. The model is live on the company's Tinker cloud service, with weights due next week under an open-source licence. Around the same time, Business Insider reported the company is raising a $5 billion round led by Accel at a $40 billion valuation.
items.source: SiliconANGLE（据 Thinking Machines 与 Business Insider）

items.title: Anthropic's Project EVE: Claude agents profit in markets but can't catch a saboteur teammate
items.summary: Anthropic published Project EVE research on Nov 6 (with game maker Fenris Creations, from its Fellows Program, April–July): Claude agents profited steadily in simulated EVE Online markets — Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 were profitable in all nine two-week windows, Fable 5 gaining about 43% per window and roughly 600% over six months (versus about 200% for Opus 4.6), mostly by independently adopting spread-capture strategies; but when asked to predict price direction, even Fable 5 profited only about half the time. The other half of the study is more striking: in four-agent EVE Frontier teams, a teammate explicitly instructed to secretly sabotage the mission was almost never identified — only one honest agent in one Opus 4.8 run definitively named the saboteur, and dedicated monitors reading only the public channel caught just 30–40%, never with more than 50% confidence. Anthropic stresses this tests sabotage on instruction, not spontaneous malice; the conclusion is that profitable execution and mutual oversight are not the same thing, and accountability for agent teams remains an open problem.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources four Cosmos 3 Nano world-model checkpoints with synchronized video and LiDAR
items.summary: NVIDIA released four 16B open-weight Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints on Hugging Face on Nov 5: Transfer-Auto (offline multi-view driving data generation, up to 11 camera views including fisheyes, with joint video and LiDAR generation), Sim-Auto (streaming driving simulation), Sim-Transfer (rendering physics-simulator output as photorealistic video) and Sim-Bimanual (bimanual robot action prediction, for YAM and AgiBot platforms). All four permit commercial use under the OpenMDW1.1 licence and ship with post-training recipes and inference examples; NVIDIA also stresses the generated output still needs to be validated in practice and cannot be treated as real sensor data.
items.source: Hugging Face 官方博客（据英伟达发布）

items.title: Wuzhen Summit: first Global Open AI Action Initiative; agents to get verifiable IDs
items.summary: The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit closed on Nov 5 with the first Global Open AI Action Initiative (18 action items across open development, safety and trustworthiness, dialogue and governance, and mutual benefit and inclusion), plus a self-discipline convention on AI agent development proposing layered, verifiable agent identities, permission controls and rule embedding — once agents can place orders, sign contracts and call other agents for a user, the system must answer who acted, with what authority, and who is accountable. The same day underscored China's AI scale: Kimi K3.1 Pro and ERNIE 5.5 Flash open weights, video-model startup Sand.ai announcing a $200M Series A+ that takes its ten-month total to $300M and unicorn status, and Kuaishou-backed chip startup Lingchuan closing a 1 billion yuan Series B.

items.title: Moonshot open-sources Kimi K3.1 Pro weights: 2.8T parameters, a 1.56 TB download (released Nov 4, catch-up)
items.summary: Moonshot released the full Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Nov 4 as promised: a 2.8T-parameter MoE with 104B active per token, a 1M-token context and text-plus-image input; the download is 1.56 TB (96 safetensors files, MXFP4-quantized) and running it needs at least eight data-center GPUs. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, close to Claude Opus 5.5's 66.4% (vendor-measured), and it ranks first among open-weights models on Agent Arena. The licence is custom, not standard open source: model-as-a-service providers earning over $20M a year must sign a separate deal, and products with over 100M monthly users or $20M monthly revenue must display 'Kimi K3.1-Pro' prominently.
items.source: The AI News Report（据 Hugging Face 模型卡）

items.title: Grok API starts watermarking text by default today, for the EU AI Act
items.summary: xAI's developer docs: from November 7, the Grok API applies an invisible watermark by default to text from seven models — grok-4.7, 4.6, 4.5, 4.3 and three grok-4.20 variants — covering plain text, structured outputs and tool-call arguments on every endpoint. Nothing is added to the text and there is no extra cost or speed impact; detection returns 'watermarked', 'not watermarked' or 'uncertain'. The stated reason is a single line: to comply with Article 50 of the EU AI Act (in force since August 2). Only team admins can switch it off per model, confirming a legal exception applies and accepting sole responsibility for marking. Anthropic started watermarking four older Claude models on Tuesday; OpenAI says it will watermark ChatGPT only in the EU.

items.title: [Issue 03 tracking update] New paper: decision models as policy gates for coding agents — Jev recall rises to 98.2%
items.summary: A November 1 arXiv paper evaluated 22 hosted decision models and two prompted general models as policy gates for coding agents: writing 28 rules as examples and counterexamples lifted risky-action recall by 5.5–26.1 points on all 23 available models and cut false positives on 21; Jev 1.14's recall rose from 89.3% to 98.2%, unnecessary interruptions fell from 30.6% to 4.8% of 252 clean actions, at 120 ms median latency and $0.46 per thousand requests. It is more evidence of Jev landing in real agent safety loops: decision models are not only routing and triage, they are starting to gate whether an agent may take a step at all. The author cautions the dataset is synthetic (2,643 tool calls) and the findings await replication in real settings.
